previous_statement: Convergence, exactness, and the unit. Choose a_corr>0 so K_N*a_corr<=1/4, 6*a_corr<1, and 7*a_corr<1. Starting with S_0=T, apply node 1.2.2 recursively. With b_0<=a and b_{k+1}<=K_N*b_k^2, one has b_k<=a*2^{-k}; the telescoping estimate ||S_{k+1}-S_k||_cb<=3b_k gives ||S_k-S_0||_cb<=6a<1, so node 1.2.1 and ||S_0||_cb<=2 imply ||S_k||_cb<=3 and justify every iteration. Thus S_k converges in cb norm to one dagger-preserving linear map mu with ||mu-T||_cb<=6a. Passing to the limit gives mu(xy)=mu(x)mu(y), and amplification commutes with the limit, so ||mu_n-T_n||<=6a for all n. Also ||mu(I)-I||<=7a<1. Since mu(I) is a self-adjoint idempotent in B(H), either mu(I)=I or I-mu(I) is a nonzero projection of norm one; the strict bound forces mu(I)=I. Thus node 1.2 holds with C_corr=6 and this universal a_corr.
new_statement: Convergence and exactness. Choose a_corr>0 so K_N*c_u*a_corr<=1/2 and 6*c_u*a_corr<1. Start from the exactly unital S_0 of node 1.2.1 and apply node 1.2.2 recursively. With b_0<=c_u*a and b_{k+1}<=K_N*b_k^2, one has b_k<=b_0*2^{-k}. Thus ||S_k-S_0||_cb<=sum_k 3b_k<=6c_u*a; after decreasing a_corr, ||S_k||_cb<=3, so every iteration is justified. The sequence converges in cb norm to one unital dagger-preserving linear map mu, and passing to the limit gives mu(xy)=mu(x)mu(y). Moreover ||mu-T||_cb<=||S_0-T||_cb+||mu-S_0||_cb<=(1+6c_u)a, and amplification commutes with the limit. Hence node 1.2 holds with the universal C_corr=1+6c_u=43, using the same level-one mu at all n.
